hook: Alexander the Great's teacher, who wrote about almost everything and founded logic and biology.

pages.t: A doctor's son from the north
pages.x: Aristotle was born in 384 BC in Stagira, in northern Greece, the son of the doctor to the king of Macedon. At 17 he went to Athens and studied at Plato's Academy for twenty years. Plato is said to have called him "the mind of the school".

In 343 BC King Philip II of Macedon hired him to teach his 13-year-old son, Alexander. They studied politics, medicine and Homer. Years later, while conquering Persia, Alexander slept with a copy of the Iliad marked up by Aristotle under his pillow, next to a dagger.

Back in Athens in 335 BC he opened his own school, the Lyceum, with a great library and collections of plants and animals. He liked to teach while strolling along its covered walk, so his followers were called the Peripatetics, "the ones who walk around".
Aristotle worked out rules for sound reasoning, like the syllogism: all men are mortal; Socrates is a man; so Socrates is mortal.
pages.fx: His logic was the standard for 2,000 years and is the ancestor of the formal logic that runs mathematics and every computer program.

pages.x: He studied and described more than 500 kinds of animals, and noticed that dolphins breathe air and feed their young on milk, and that octopuses change colour.
pages.fx: He is called the father of biology. Darwin said the great naturalists of his own day were "mere schoolboys to old Aristotle".

pages.x: He also got things famously wrong: that heavy things fall faster than light ones, that we think with the heart, that women have fewer teeth than men. People trusted him so much that some of these mistakes lasted until Galileo and others tested them, nearly 2,000 years later.
pages.img: Galileo's Leaning Tower of Pisa experiment

pages.x: When Alexander died in 323 BC, anger against Macedon boiled over in Athens and Aristotle was charged with insulting the gods. Remembering Socrates, he fled, saying he would not let Athens "sin twice against philosophy". He died the next year on the island of Euboea.

Aristotle wrote on logic, physics, biology, ethics, politics, poetry and more. To Muslim scholars he was "the First Teacher", to medieval Europe simply "the Philosopher", and many fields he named are still studied.
pts: Shaped Islamic and Christian thought for 1,500 years
